chapter: Broadway, tenors, Billie Holiday and Rhythm Club memories
title: Don Byas

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Did you know Don Byas very well?
Oh God yeah, I just saw him before he died.
Sure.
You mean when he was back in this country.
Oh yeah.
Where did you see him?
In New York and saw him in Chicago. I was
one of the first ones he called when he was there making some records with, what the devil is his name, for Dan Morgan.....
There was TV show that I saw, you know he sounded good. A friend of mine heard him around that time, but he didn't sound so good. How did he sound to you?
He sounded good to me that day, he wasn't drinking, you know.
Yeah, he sounded great on the TV show.
Don Byas.
He started to drink again?
Yeah.
By the time you saw him. Because I guess when he was in Europe he was just totally on the wagon.
Yeah, he was really ... he was doing scuba diving and all that, he was doing great, got back over here and started drinking. It's too bad.
Temperamentally he was a pretty aggressive guy, right?
Yeah, yeah, oh goodness he's been on so many recordings of mine. One of them was one of Foots Thomas' originals 'Buy Us a Drink.' Don Byas, great tenor player.
No question, yeah.
Got a picture of him, Don Byas, Coleman Hawkins and Thelonious Monk.
From 52nd Street, huh?
